# Real saved example (offline)

These files contain one real, rights-checked publication. Synthetic provider
fixtures are created inside tests and never appear in the browser's saved mode.

**Zheng QX, Wang HW, Ge L, Lin Y, Gao X, Zhu Y, Huang L, Jiang XM (2026).**
*Influences of dietary intake on Chinese women with gestational diabetes mellitus
by inhibiting gut microbiome on plasma metabolome.* Frontiers in Immunology.
[DOI 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1745459](https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1745459),
[PMID 42051515](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42051515/),
[PMC13110953](https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13110953).

Copyright © 2026 Zheng, Wang, Ge, Lin, Gao, Zhu, Huang and Jiang.
Distributed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
The CORE metadata reports `cc by`, and the article's own XML permissions link
to that same license. The XML contains the expected own PMID, PMCID and DOI.
No images, publisher pages, PDFs, or restricted full text were downloaded.

`manifest.json` records the exact Europe PMC query, actual response-file capture
time, source URL, XML retrieval time, author attribution, license, SHA-256
checksums, transformations and scope. The search reported **9** matches and
returned **2** metadata records. Only this one CC BY article was retained;
the other article was CC BY-NC and was excluded by the conservative MVP policy.
No full search response or excluded article abstract is bundled here.

`PMC13110953.xml` is the unchanged UTF-8 Europe PMC `fullTextXML` response.
`PMC13110953.metadata.json` is only the selected CORE result, reformatted as
sorted, indented JSON. The citation abstract is extracted from this same CC BY
XML. Canonical passages use the existing `lit-rev-engine.source.v1.jats_xml`
parser, which normalizes XML whitespace and represents table rows using tabs.

This is a **curated saved example**, not a new PubMed search, a complete capture,
a systematic review, or a scientific conclusion. It explicitly concerns the
reported Chinese pregnant controls and participants with gestational diabetes.
Study location does not establish ethnicity; this fixture does not support a
general claim about all Asian women. The question remains editable for passage
search and human assessment.
